content.comment:
Hi,
Thanks a lot for your comment.

First of all, the provided code is intentionally using CPU (and not GPU) to let everyone use and try it. As mentioned in the paper, MDE reaches 99% of its ranking performance in 100 iterations, and MDE_NN reaches its best performance in the benchmarks after just 50 iterations. Therefore it does not require a GPU cluster to run for most of the applications. 
Moreover, please note that we will release soon the GPU version (after the conference deadline), as pushing a new code release during the reviewing phase could be perceived as a conference policy violation. However, in case you would like to train the model yourself on GPU before our next release, you could use the   .cuda method available in Pytorch.

To answer your second point,  MDE_Model.py contains the "MDE model" and MDE_NN_Model.py contains the "MDE_NN" model.  We provide more details about them in the paper: in Section 4 and 4.1.

The training experiment set (provided with the submission) runs the test after every 50 iterations, therefore it includes the testing as well and you do not need to run tests separately. So to run the training and the testing experiment on WN18RR you can just run the program with the following argument: “-t train -d WN18RR”. Where “-t” represents the task and “-d” represents the dataset. 

In particular,  “-t test”  is for when the model is once trained and stored using the save() method (line 394). To make this argument work replace the train_experiment in line 796 to test_experimen and enable saving a model at training time by enabling the commented save() method in line 394. 

Please, do not hesitate to ask us for more details.
Best regards

display_title: Some concerns about the source code

content.comment:
Hi, 
I ran the code and found that the training process of MDE_NN is strange. Some concerns about the source code are as follows. 

(1) I noticed that MDE_NN uses a sigmoid layer, so the score of any triple can never be greater than 1.0. However, you set the hyperparameters gamma_1 and gamma_2 to 2 for the WN18RR, and 9 for the FB15K237 dataset. Hence, the losses of positive triples are always 0, which means that the positive triples will have no effect on the parameter optimization. 

(2) In early training stages, due to the hyperparameter settings in (1), most of the triples have the same score: 1.0. According to the ranking method in the source code, for a link prediction task (h, r, ?), the positive triple (h, r, t*) is likely to have a high rank (since most of the candidate triples have the same score: 1.0). This leads to the high MRR and Hits@N in early training stages.

Thanks and regards

content.title: The MDE_NN extension in the training
content.comment:
Thanks for the comments. 

The gamma_1 and gamma_2 hyperparameters of MDE are greater than the range of the logistic function and replacing the logistic function in the code with tanhshrink resolves the mentioned behavior of MDE_NN 
 in the training. This fix, however, invalidates the reported results for the neural network extension of MDE (MDE_NN).  
Our tests show using tanhshrink MDE_NN gives about the results of MDE. Therefore the benefit of the MDE_NN extension is to reduce the number of hyperparameters of MDE by learning them as the multiplier weights.

Kind regards
